evidence.title: CertiK, V Systems and ZICO Sign MOU to Advance Institutional Tokenization Across Greater China and ASEAN
evidence.body: [e001:f01] The MOU was signed at Cyberport during a session of the Cyberport Venture Capital Forum (CVCF) 2026 at Hong Kong FinTech Week. [e001:f02] Under the MOU, the parties intend to combine their respective expertise. [e001:f03] V Systems builds modular, institution-grade blockchain infrastructure and tokenization platforms for banks, sovereign-level investors and regulated financial institutions. [e001:f04] CertiK, the largest Web3 security services provider, brings blockchain security expertise, including smart contract audits, formal verification, penetration testing, Proof of Reserves, and on-chain monitoring through Skynet. [e001:f05] ZICO is a full-service Malaysian law firm with an established practice in fintech, digital assets and capital markets, including advisory work on tokenized capital market instruments and payment systems. [e001:f06] The collaboration builds on an established track record in institutional tokenization and blockchain security. [e001:f07] V Systems served as the technology platform provider for Malaysia’s first tokenized sukuk, priced by Khazanah Nasional Berhad in 2026. [e001:f08] CertiK has also provided independent security assessments for blockchain systems delivered by V Systems for regulated financial institutions in Malaysia and Singapore. [e001:f09] “We see Greater China and ASEAN as key growth engines for institutional tokenization,” said YK Goh, CEO of Coded Solution Limited (V Systems). [e001:f10] “Through this MOU, we are establishing a partnership to make blockchain infrastructure more scalable, strengthen security and improve cross-border interoperability. [e001:f11] Islamic finance is one such opportunity, and Malaysia’s well-established Islamic finance framework gives us a strong foundation to build on.” “Institutional tokenization is reaching an inflection point across ASEAN and Greater China, driven by growing appetite for real-world asset tokenization and cross-border capital liquidity,” said Jonathan Lim, Managing Partner at Zaid Ibrahim & Co. [e001:f12] “Connecting regional digital asset initiatives requires aligning technical resilience, on-chain security, and multi-jurisdictional clarity. [e001:f13] This strategic collaboration creates a powerful catalyst to unlock institutional participation and streamline cross-market execution for digital financial instruments across both regions.” “As banks and sovereign-level institutions move tokenization into production, security has to be built in from the start,” said Esme Pau, Head of Capital Markets and Policy at CertiK. [e001:f14] “Working with V Systems and ZICO, we aim to help institutions address security and regulatory needs early and prepare tokenized products for cross-market deployment.” About CertiK CertiK is the largest Web3 security services provider and a trusted risk management partner for regulators, institutions, and Web3 innovators worldwide. [e001:f15] Since 2017, CertiK has protected over $600 billion in digital assets across 150+ countries and regions, while providing full-lifecycle security and risk management solutions for institutional clients. [e001:f16] Operating under SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 standards, CertiK works closely with regulators worldwide on digital asset policy development and regulatory consultation.

evidence.title: Nasdaq sees worst day in 19 months as investors bet on AI slowdown after Democrats’ election triumph
evidence.body: [e001:f01] As Wall Street sustained widespread losses, the [Nasdaq](https:// composite tumbled into “correction territory” – more than 10% below its recent record high – with more than $2tn shaved off its value by the end of trading Thursday. [e001:f02] The tech-heavy index had its biggest one-day fall since Donald Trump announced his “liberation day” tariffs on US trading partners in April 2025. [e001:f03] The Latest Worries over massive AI spending gripped the New York stock market and rippled out to other bourses worldwide as investors anticipated tougher scrutiny of datacentre expansion plans. [e001:f04] Chip stocks led the slump, with memory maker SanDisk tumbling by 22% and hard drive maker Western Digital falling by 17%. [e001:f05] Wall Street’s “fear index”, the VIX, jumped by 61% to its highest levels since the early weeks of the Iran war, in a sign of rising market volatility. [e001:f06] The heavy falls continued in Asia on Friday, with Japan’s Nikkei 225 index sinking 6% and South Korea’s Kospi index tumbling more than 8% in early trading. [A chart showing how the ‘fear index’ has risen after the midterms](https:// Analysts pointed to expectations that Democratic governors will [clamp down on the rollout of new datacentres](https:// after the party won a series of gubernatorial races this week. [e001:f07] Neil Wilson, investor strategist at Saxo UK, said a “complete capitulation-level event” was playing out in tech stocks on Thursday. [e001:f08] “The fear is a total momentum unwind as Democrats pace the frontier and kibosh datacentre buildout … this looks totally overdone but the nature of ‘sell everything’ in this market means we need to look for some stability first,” Wilson said. [e001:f09] The [Dow Jones](https:// industrial average (DJIA) of 30 large US companies was down more than 1,800 points by the end of the day, a fall of 3.4%, to 51,868 points. [e001:f10] The S&P 500 was down 4.3%. [A chart showing how the S&P 500 and Nasdaq have tumbled after the midterms](https:// Nvidia, the chipmaker at the heart of the AI boom, was the top faller on the DJIA – down 9.2%, followed by Goldman Sachs, which fell 3.7%. [e001:f11] An early stock market rally in Europe had fizzled out by late trading, with Britain’s FTSE 100 closing down 46 points or 0.4% at 10782.66. [e001:f12] The sell-off is a sharp reverse of Wednesday’s rally, when Wall Street stocks had their biggest daily gain in months as investors anticipated that the Democratic party’s success in the US midterm elections could restrain the White House. [e001:f13] The president wrote on Truth Social: “Stock Market just hit another Record High – 91 Days in just a short period of time – Less than two years. [e001:f14] TRUMP.” Tech analyst Dan Ives has warned that the results of the midterms are a clear sign that the pace of datacentre buildout will start to slow down. [e001:f15] “There is no way to sugarcoat that Democrats taking control, especially over the Senate, will create some major hurdles for AI and tech legislation in the Beltway over the next two years,” Ives said. [e001:f16] “The market’s moving from the promise ⁠of AI to the price of AI,” said Ted Parkhill, founder and CEO of Incline ​Investment Management.

evidence.title: Investors wipe $2.5trln off Nasdaq as blue tsunami prompts AI fears
evidence.body: [e006:f01] Tech-led Nasdaq notched its deepest one-day drop since ‘Liberation Day’ in April 2025, wiping out trillions in market value on fears of more AI scrutiny, particularly on data center construction, after Democrats won big in US midterm elections. [e006:f02] The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5% on investor fears that the Democratic Party's sweeping midterm victory could stall AI infrastructure expansion and force a reckoning for smaller firms whose capacity to raise funds has already been limited by higher interest rates and tighter financial conditions. [e006:f03] It was the second straight day of selling in AI stocks and the fifth decline of more than 500 points in the Nasdaq Composite since mid-October, as the previously buoyant AI trade has come under increasing scrutiny in the last several weeks. [e006:f04] The Nasdaq Composite is now in correction territory, having lost nearly 12% from its record close on October 6. [e006:f05] Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi have risen more than 20% this year, but they fell significantly following Wednesday's rout in data center shares. [e006:f06] Some analysts wondered if the scale of the wipeout could affect the timing of Anthropic's blockbuster IPO expected this fall, as any delay could amplify market sentiment. [e006:f07] The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index fell 12% to touch its lowest level in more than six months. [e006:f08] Nvidia dropped 9% and Advanced Micro slumped 17%. [e006:f09] Wall Street's fear gauge, the VIX index of expected price swings, posted its largest increase since December 2024. [e006:f10] The Nasdaq 100 index, composed of the biggest names in the broader index, fell 6.4%, erasing $2.5 trillion in market value. [e006:f11] The selling suggests investors are starting to factor in increased local opposition to the data center buildout, with some analysts saying markets have yet to fully consider the costs it has imposed on US communities. [e006:f12] There's going to be a difficult road to get those permitted forthcoming." Around 30% of expected US data center capacity additions in 2028 could be at risk from potential construction pauses, UBS analysts estimated, threatening an industry whose growth depends on a rapid buildout of new facilities. [e006:f13] AI WINNERS WILT Neocloud company CoreWeave, which has become a barometer of investor anxiety over heavy AI spending and borrowing, slumped 10%. [e006:f14] Spreads on Intel's 5-year credit default swaps also hit a record 149.7 bps. [e006:f15] Shares of both firms have dropped by half or more since the Nasdaq Composite hit a record on October 6. [e006:f16] GE Vernova fell 7.4%, while Constellation Energy slipped 2.5%.
